video.title: Exposing The Initial Yahoo Fantasy Basketball Rankings For Fantasy Basketball

summary: Josh Lloyd reviews Yahoo's first fantasy basketball rankings for the 2026-27 season. He explains why they matter: Yahoo is the most-used platform and its rankings shape ADP. He also points out that Yahoo's X-rank does not match any single format. He goes through the top 25, mostly agreeing at the very top. He thinks Tyrese Maxey, Jalen Johnson, Donovan Mitchell, Kawhi Leonard, Chet Holmgren, Alperen Sengun and Walker Kessler are ranked too high. He fades Kon Knueppel, Jalen Brunson, Alex Sarr, Donovan Clingan, Mikal Bridges, Payton Pritchard and AJ Dybantsa. He buys Amen Thompson, Dejounte Murray, Dyson Daniels, Austin Reaves, Jaden McDaniels, Matas Buzelis and Jakob Poeltl. In close head-to-head picks he takes Giannis over Jalen Johnson, Lauri Markkanen over Desmond Bane, and Paul George over Jarrett Allen.

rules.text: Yahoo rankings matter because Yahoo is the most-used platform and its rankings drive ADP in mock and real drafts. Use them as a baseline for where players will go.
rules.quote: And the rankings influence the ADP. So you go into a mockdraft, you go into a real draft

rules.text: Yahoo's X-rank is a vibes-based list that ignores your league format. The draft room defaults to it. The separate 'rank' column is built from statistical projections and changes with your league settings.
rules.quote: X-rank is the vibes based ranking. rank is based on what their statistical projections are

rules.text: Ranking players by nine-cat totals is the worst way to rank them.
rules.quote: because they base it on, you know, the worst way to rank players, nine cat totals.

rules.text: Yahoo's default roster uses two centers. You should always change it. Yahoo also still has no third round reversal option.
rules.quote: they still have two centers as their default, which you should always change

rules.text: This season Yahoo correctly combines weeks seven and eight into one matchup for the NBA Cup.
rules.quote: They have combined weeks seven and eight into one matchup to become week seven, which is correct.

rules.text: Watch out for players whose team has a two-game fantasy playoff week. It can be a tiebreaker but should not override a clear talent gap.
rules.quote: the twoame playoff week wouldn't change my opinion on that

rules.text: Avoid one-year blindness. Do not let one season flip a long-term narrative such as a player being injury prone or reliable.
rules.quote: people have one year blindness or one year narrow focus, one year tunnels.

rules.text: The further down the draft board you go, the less the gaps between slots matter. A gap between picks 1 and 20 is huge. A gap between 50 and 70 is small.
rules.quote: the further down we get the draft board, the differences in positions become less important.

rules.text: Points league and category league values can differ a lot. Use rankings that match your format.
rules.quote: this one is dependent on on format. This is why why I talk about coherence.

rules.text: Players often slow down the year after a long championship run because they are exhausted.
rules.quote: Many of these guys slow down in the year after the championship. They have to pull back

rules.text: Steals swing from year to year. A drop from three to two steals cuts a third of a player's value in that category, and it can bounce back.
rules.quote: steals change all the time." He went from three steals to two steals, losing 33% of his value

rules.text: Value is relative to where a player is drafted. Fading or buying a player depends on his price, not on liking or disliking him.
rules.quote: It's all about relativity because last season there were times when Dyson Daniels was being discussed

rules.text: Think about team build when choosing between players: positional need, which centers are left, and how much injury risk you already have.
rules.quote: there's team build ideas. Do I need a center? What other centers are available?

rules.text: Winning fantasy leagues comes down to finding players who can jump 40 spots above their draft position.
rules.quote: winning fantasy leagues, if you want to boil it down to one thing, it's finding someone who can jump 40 spots.
